title: Console omnibar + persistent saved searches for audit viewer with cursored pagination and diagnostic CSV/JSON exports
creator: Ava Patel
body:
Summary:
We need a unified omnibar in the Console audit viewer that lets operators run ad-hoc queries, apply multi-field filters, and persist/save a search. Saved searches should be shareable, editable, and appear in a new "Saved Queries" sidebar. Results must support cursored pagination (stable ordering) for reliable exports. Export functionality should let admins export the current result set to CSV or JSON with a diagnostic mode that adds metadata columns (request_id, model_variant, routed_region, rule_fallback, matched_policy) while respecting RBAC v2 and field-level redaction rules.

Problem / Motivation:
- Current viewer search is fragmented: filters live in multiple controls, and exports are limited to small page sizes which leads to inconsistent slices when results shift during export.
- Teams need repeatable saved queries for audits and pager investigations.
- Exports used for compliance require contextual diagnostic fields for post-incident analysis but must not leak PII or secrets.
- RBAC v2 adds role-aware column visibility; export must enforce field-level permissions and log export events into audit logs.

Goals / Non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Single omnibar for quick text search + filter tokens + date ranges + freeform Kibana-like syntax fallback.
  - Persistent saved searches (name, owner, visibility: private/team/org).
  - Cursored pagination API to enable deterministic exports of large result sets without skipping/duplication.
  - Export CSV/JSON with optional "diagnostic" toggles; admin-only diagnostic columns enforced by RBAC v2.
  - Audit export events (who exported what, when, filters used) are themselves logged to the audit stream.
- Non-goals:
  - Full-text indexing overhaul — use existing ES/Clickhouse indexes.
  - Long-running async export jobs in this ticket (we will support streaming exports up to 100k rows; separate ticket for multi-day archival jobs).

Acceptance criteria:
- Omnibar implemented in Console header for audit viewer with tokenized filter UX and fallback syntax parser.
- Users can save a search with metadata (name, description, visibility). Saved searches listed in sidebar and can be applied or edited.
- API endpoint /audit/search supports cursor param (opaque token) and returns stable next_cursor; results identical across pages when no writes occur.
- Export button on result set opens options: format (CSV|JSON), rows limit, include diagnostics (admin-only).
- Export enforces RBAC v2 visibility rules: columns redacted client-side and server-side; attempts to access denied columns return 403.
- Export events create a new audit-event record containing export metadata (search_id or filter snapshot, requester, format, row_count).
- Unit + integration tests covering: saved search CRUD, cursor pagination edge cases, RBAC enforcement on export, export event logging.

Implementation notes / approach:
- Frontend: React omnibar component integrated into AuditViewer container. Tokenized input with chips for fields (actor:, action:, resource:, region:, outcome:, timestamp:). "Save search" modal with visibility selector. Saved searches persisted to Console metadata store (new table saved_audit_searches).
- Backend: Reuse existing audit-query service but add a cursor layer: when a query executes, we snapshot the sort keys (timestamp desc, event_id) and return an opaque cursor that includes last seen key and query hash. The search API will accept cursor and limit.
- Export: For results <10k rows return inline export; for larger results stream chunks, returning a signed URL from object store. Diagnostic columns pulled from correlated metadata table. Enforce RBAC via middleware that filters requested columns server-side before serialization. Also redact values for fields marked sensitive in config (PII fields list).
- RBAC v2 interactions: saved searches with visibility = "team" will be validated against team membership via RBAC. Diagnostic exports require role export_privilege.
- Telemetry: emit events for saved_search.created, saved_search.used, export.requested with metadata.
- Migrations: create saved_audit_searches table with columns: id, org_id, owner_id, team_id, name, description, visibility, query_blob, created_at, updated_at.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag omnibar and saved searches per org. Default off for existing orgs.
- Beta with internal orgs then staged rollout to customers.

Open questions & trade-offs:
- Cursor format: opaque token vs server-side snapshot ID. Opaque token preferred to avoid retention complexity but may grow token size.
- Export scale: do we require async job for >100k rows? We will cap inline/streamed export at 100k and introduce background archival export in a follow-up.
- Visibility semantics for saved searches: should team visibility map to RBAC teams or Console teams? For now map to RBAC team IDs.

Links to artifacts and references:
- Design sketches: https://drive.google.com/designs/omnibar-audit-v2
- API RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/r/audit-omnibar-rfc
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-24011 (query-fabrication), ENG-34677 (live-tail snapshot exports)
comments: 2025-02-11 — Luca Moretti: Spiked on cursor implementation; prototype uses (timestamp, event_id) ordering and encodes last seen key + query hash in base64. Need to confirm retention implications if underlying events get compacted.
2025-02-12 — Priya Nair (PM): UX reviewed. Add 'share link' for saved searches that encodes a safe snapshot id. Also ensure we show 'last run' and 'last run by' in the saved searches list.
2025-02-14 — Security review (notes): Redaction config must be centrally controllable via KMS-backed config. Diagnostic columns require explicit approval; mark ticket security_review_required=true.

2025-02-17 — Design feedback (Marcos Silva): Make diagnostic columns opt-in with explanatory tooltip. For CSV, include header of redaction status (e.g., 'email (redacted)') so auditors know what was removed.

2025-02-19 — Engineering update (Luca): Backend cursor endpoint implemented behind ff_audit_omnibar. Integration tests for cursor stability added. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8421
2025-02-20 — QA (Riley Chen): Found edge case when query includes both sort override and cursor: if client overrides sort we currently reject with 400; document this in API spec and bubble UX error.
